doc.title: Candido Camero — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

chapter: To the US and the Caribbean with Carmen and Rolando
title: La Conga, Chano Pozo and Cacha, and the touring route again
summary: He confirms the route Havana Madrid, Chicago, La Conga, and that Chano Pozo and Cacha joined the Miguelito Valdes show, then Puerto Rico and Santo Domingo.

story.theme_name: Life on the road: touring bands, buses and one-nighters
story.community_name: Life on the road: buses, trains and one-nighters

blocks.x: Then you came to United States for the first time with the dance couple Carmen and Rolando in 1946 to perform at the Havana Madrid. Camero In the Havana Madrid.
Then you all went to the Conga Club. Camero No. Before the Conga we went to Chicago - to the Latin Quarter of Chicago.
Ya. Camero After the Habana Madrid, we went to Chicago. Then we returned from Chicago to La Conga.

And there you replaced another dancing couple made up of Cacha and Chano Pozo. Camero Well, they came later. We were . . . the show was made up of . . . Miguelito Valdés, he was the star of the show. So in that show we were Carmen and Rolando, I was the bongo player for them, then came Chano with Pepe and Cacha. Cacha was Chano’s wife and Pepe was Cacha’s dance partner. After there well, then we left when the contract was up. Chano went to work alone. The couple went one way and Chano another. He joined Katherine Dunham’s Afro- Cuban company.

At the Roxie hotel here in New York. And we went to Puerto Rico to the Escambrón Beach Club. After Puerto Rico, well we were there six months. Then we went to Santo Domingo. We were there touring the entire republic. A very good show, very good.
